claims.text: The starting material is an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy in a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
Mo, Nb, Ta, or W should be introduced into the alloy composition.
Adding the proposed refractory elements will promote formation of a BCC solid-solution phase.
The refractory-element-containing solid solution will be stable.
Adding refractory elements will reduce the formation of intermetallic compounds.
Formation of a stable solid solution and suppression of intermetallic compounds will increase strength.
Formation of a stable solid solution and suppression of intermetallic compounds will improve corrosion resistance.
Formation of a stable solid solution and suppression of intermetallic compounds will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Refractory-element addition will improve strength relative to the as-processed baseline.
Refractory-element addition will improve ductility relative to the as-processed baseline.
Refractory-element addition will improve corrosion resistance relative to the as-processed baseline.
Refractory-element addition will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-processed baseline.
Refractory-element addition will improve the combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance.
The optimal amount and combination of refractory elements and their microstructural effects are uncertain.
Mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance should be measured across alloys containing different amounts and combinations of refractory elements.
Failure of refractory-element additions to improve combined mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation performance would falsify the hypothesis.
